segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we're talking a little bit about food and about your health.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们正在谈论一些关于食物和你的健康的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to take a look at our favorite maybe kind of food.
segments.zh: 今天我们要看看我们最喜欢的食物。

segments.en: We're taking a look at the fast food, all these yummy but not very healthy types of food.
segments.zh: 我们正在看看快餐，所有这些美味但不是很健康的食物。

segments.en: Yeah, we are.
segments.zh: 是的，我们是。

segments.en: So let's listen to our dialogue and when we come back we'll be talking about what some of these foods are and what some of the phrases you've heard mean.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听我们的对话，当我们回来时，我们会谈论这些食物中的一些是什么以及你听到的一些短语是什么意思。

segments.en: I'm hungry.
segments.zh: 我饿了。

segments.en: Let's order up something to eat.
segments.zh: 点点东西吃吧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Maybe we can order a soup and a salad from the restaurant down the street.
segments.zh: 要不从街角那家餐厅点份汤和沙拉？

segments.en: I was thinking of getting a hamburger, fries and a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 我倒想点汉堡、薯条和巧克力圣代。

segments.en: You eat too much junk food.
segments.zh: 你垃圾食品吃得太多了。

segments.en: That sort of stuff clogs up your arteries and is very high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 这些东西容易堵塞动脉，胆固醇含量也很高。

segments.en: Well I never seem to gain weight so I don't mind.
segments.zh: 反正我好像怎么吃都不胖，无所谓。

segments.en: It's not only about getting fat or not, it's about being healthy.
segments.zh: 这不只是胖不胖的问题，还关系到健康。

segments.en: You could really have some health problems later on.
segments.zh: 以后你真可能出健康问题。

segments.en: How about pizza or maybe some fried chicken?
segments.zh: 那点披萨或炸鸡怎么样？

segments.en: Better yet, let's order some hot dogs.
segments.zh: 要不干脆点热狗！

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at language takeaway.
segments.zh: 现在来看看“语言要点”。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So first up on language takeaway is a very unhealthy food.
segments.zh: 所以首先在语言要点是一种非常不健康的食物。

segments.en: It's called a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 它被称为巧克力圣代。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We wanted to order hamburger, french fries and a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 我们想点汉堡包、炸薯条和巧克力圣代。

segments.en: So chocolate we know that this is the flavor that comes from cocoa.
segments.zh: 所以巧克力我们知道这是可可的味道。

segments.en: But what is a sundae?
segments.zh: 但什么是圣代？

segments.en: Well basically a sundae is a kind of ice cream dessert.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上圣代是一种冰淇淋甜点。

segments.en: It comes in a cup or a bowl and it's usually vanilla ice cream with chocolate sauce and then oftentimes a cherry on top.
segments.zh: 它装在杯子或碗里，通常是香草冰淇淋和巧克力酱，然后通常是樱桃。

segments.en: So as you can see the word is pronounced exactly like the day, sundae, but it has a different spelling in the end.
segments.zh: 正如你所看到的，这个词的发音和 day 完全一样，sundae，但结尾的拼写不同。

segments.en: S-U-N-D-A-E, sundae.
segments.zh: S-U-N-D-A-E，圣代。

segments.en: So this is a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个巧克力圣代。

segments.en: So when you see this spelling, a sundae with an E, that's the dessert.
segments.zh: 所以当你看到这个拼写时，一个带有 E 的圣代，这就是甜点。

segments.en: If you see it with a Y, that's the day.
segments.zh: 如果你看到的是带 Y 的拼写，那就是 day（天）。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So chocolate sundae, actually a very delicious dessert, but remember it's ice cream.
segments.zh: 所以巧克力圣代，实际上是一种非常美味的甜点，但请记住它是冰淇淋。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And all of these types of food, hamburger, chocolate sundae, it's called junk food.
segments.zh: 还有所有这些类型的食物，汉堡包，巧克力圣代，它被称为垃圾食品。

segments.en: Junk food.
segments.zh: 垃圾食品。

segments.en: Well food you know.
segments.zh: 你知道的食物。

segments.en: Junk.
segments.zh: 垃圾。

segments.en: What is an example of junk, Marco?
segments.zh: 垃圾的例子是什么，马可？

segments.en: Well something that's not good or useful anymore.
segments.zh: 就是已经不好用、没用的东西。

segments.en: So maybe you have trash that you need to get rid of, like an old TV.
segments.zh: 所以也许你有需要摆脱的垃圾，就像一台旧电视一样。

segments.en: That's junk.
segments.zh: 那是垃圾。

segments.en: So my mom would always say, throw away this junk.
segments.zh: 所以我妈妈总是说，扔掉这个垃圾。

segments.en: It's stuff that you don't need.
segments.zh: 这是你不需要的东西。

segments.en: So junk is things that you would throw away.
segments.zh: 所以垃圾是你会扔掉的东西。

segments.en: Junk food is the kind of food that's not healthy for you.
segments.zh: 垃圾食品是一种对你不健康的食物。

segments.en: It's the food that you shouldn't eat, but it tends to be really delicious.
segments.zh: 这是你不应该吃的食物，但它往往非常美味。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So for example, the hamburger, french fries, a chocolate sundae, all this would fall under this category of junk food.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，汉堡包、炸薯条、巧克力圣代，所有这些都属于这一类垃圾食品。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And one of the things about junk food is that it's high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 垃圾食品的特点之一，就是胆固醇含量高。

segments.en: Now what is cholesterol, Marco?
segments.zh: 现在什么是胆固醇，马可？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you always have to be careful.
segments.zh: 所以你总是要小心。

segments.en: Your doctor says that you shouldn't have or you have to be careful about having high cholesterol.
segments.zh: 你的医生会说你不能有高胆固醇，或者说你得小心别让胆固醇过高。

segments.en: And that's just basically, it's a type of fat that is found in animal products.
segments.zh: 这基本上是一种在动物产品中发现的脂肪。

segments.en: So for example, beef has cholesterol and it's dangerous because it could maybe cause health problems.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，牛肉含有胆固醇，这很危险，因为它可能会导致健康问题。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So my friend needed to lower his cholesterol and his doctor told him he should eat less red meat, eat more vegetables and fruits instead.
segments.zh: 所以我的朋友需要降低他的胆固醇，他的医生告诉他应该少吃红肉，多吃蔬菜和水果。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So cholesterol is a, you'll see it all the time when you're shopping.
segments.zh: 所以胆固醇，你购物的时候经常会看到这个词。

segments.en: You'll see that it's low in cholesterol or no sugar or no calories, stuff like that.
segments.zh: 你会看到它的胆固醇含量低或没有糖或没有卡路里，诸如此类。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Now, a food that is very, very high in cholesterol is fried chicken, but it's also very delicious.
segments.zh: 现在，胆固醇非常非常高的食物是炸鸡，但它也非常美味。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Fried chicken.
segments.zh: 炸鸡。

segments.en: Now as you see, the first word there is fried and that means that it was cooked in hot oil.
segments.zh: 现在正如你所看到的，第一个词是油炸的，这意味着它是用热油烹制的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And what's important to remember about most American fried chicken is that the chicken is usually put in a batter, so like a milk, egg, flour sauce, and then it's fried.
segments.zh: 最重要的是，大多数美国炸鸡通常都放在面糊中，比如牛奶、鸡蛋、面粉酱，然后油炸。

segments.en: So on the outside it's very, very crispy and salty.
segments.zh: 所以在外面，它非常非常脆和咸。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's covered in like a type of bread, like a crispy bread.
segments.zh: 所以它外面裹着一层像面包的东西，一层酥脆的外皮。

segments.en: Yeah, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: It's usually very greasy, so when you eat it, you have lots of grease on your fingers.
segments.zh: 它通常很油腻，所以当你吃它时，你的手指上有很多油脂。

segments.en: But one of the reasons it tastes so good is because as you say, Marco, it's fried in oil.
segments.zh: 但它味道如此之好的原因之一是因为正如你所说，马可，它是用油炸的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So this is all the vocab that we have for language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以这就是我们所有的语言要点词汇。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次对话。

segments.en: I'm hungry.
segments.zh: 我饿了。

segments.en: Let's order up something to eat.
segments.zh: 点点东西吃吧。

segments.en: Okay, maybe we can order a soup and a salad from the restaurant down the street.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许我们可以从街上的餐厅点一份汤和沙拉。

segments.en: I was thinking of getting a hamburger, fries, and a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 我正在考虑买一个汉堡包、薯条和巧克力圣代。

segments.en: You eat too much junk food.
segments.zh: 你垃圾食品吃得太多了。

segments.en: That sort of stuff clogs up your arteries and is very high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 这些东西容易堵塞动脉，胆固醇含量也很高。

segments.en: Well, I never seem to gain weight, so I don't mind.
segments.zh: 好吧，我似乎从来没有体重增加，所以我不介意。

segments.en: It's not only about getting fat or not, it's about being healthy.
segments.zh: 这不只是胖不胖的问题，还关系到健康。

segments.en: You could really have some health problems later on.
segments.zh: 以后你真可能出健康问题。

segments.en: How about pizza or maybe some fried chicken?
segments.zh: 那点披萨或炸鸡怎么样？

segments.en: Better yet, let's order some hot dogs.
segments.zh: 要不干脆点热狗！

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: All right, now it's time for some phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在是关于流利表达的一些短语的时候了。

segments.en: Fluency Builder
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: So one of the first phrases is actually something that I'm excited to talk about because it comes up a lot in directions when we're giving people directions somewhere.
segments.zh: 所以第一个短语其实是我很期待讲的，因为我们在给别人指路的时候经常会用到它。

segments.en: So one of the people in the dialogue said, we can order a soup and salad from the restaurant down the street.
segments.zh: 所以对话中的一位人说，我们可以在街上的餐厅点一份汤和沙拉。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is, you're basically telling the person where the restaurant is.
segments.zh: 所以这，你基本上是在告诉对方餐厅在哪里。

segments.en: And when you say something is down the street, it means that it's nearby.
segments.zh: 当你说有什么东西在街上时，这意味着它就在附近。

segments.en: It is.
segments.zh: 确实就在附近。

segments.en: It's nearby.
segments.zh: 它在附近。

segments.en: It's on the same street or it's just a few minutes walk from where you are now.
segments.zh: 它在同一条街上，或者离你现在所在的地方只有几分钟的步行路程。

segments.en: Right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: So you can say, my apartment is just down the street from this park.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，我的公寓就在这条街上，离这个公园很近。

segments.en: So it's very close.
segments.zh: 所以非常接近。

segments.en: Or you could say, I know him.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，我认识他。

segments.en: He lived down the street from me when we were children.
segments.zh: 我们小时候，他就住在同一条街上，离我很近。

segments.en: Okay, so he lived really, really close to you.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他住得离你非常非常近。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Now, when we were talking about junk food and we were talking about how it's not healthy, we said that junk food clogs up your arteries.
segments.zh: 现在，当我们谈论垃圾食品并且谈论它不健康时，我们说垃圾食品会堵塞你的动脉。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A couple important words here to clog up arteries.
segments.zh: 这里有几个重要的词来堵塞动脉。

segments.en: The verb to clog, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 动词堵塞，这是什么意思？

segments.en: Clog with a G. It means it gets in the way or obstructs it.
segments.zh: Clog 拼写带 G。意思是挡住或阻碍了它。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So for example, if a drain, in my sink, if a drain is clogged, the water does not go down.
segments.zh: 比如，我水槽里的排水管，如果排水管堵了，水就流不下去。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So the water starts to build and build and build.
segments.zh: 所以水就开始越积越多。

segments.en: Actually, it's very dangerous because if it comes up too much, the water will go on the floor.
segments.zh: 其实这很危险，因为如果积得太多，水就会漫到地板上。

segments.en: But that's a drain, that's a sink.
segments.zh: 但这是一个排水沟，那是一个水槽。

segments.en: If you're talking about the heart, you would say that cholesterol clogs up your arteries.
segments.zh: 如果你在谈论心脏，你会说胆固醇会堵塞你的动脉。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So your arteries are like these tubes where blood passes.
segments.zh: 所以你的动脉就像这些血液通过的管子。

segments.en: And of course, if they're clogged up, then blood can't pass.
segments.zh: 当然，如果它们被堵塞了，那么血液就无法通过。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And if it's very serious, people sometimes have to have heart surgery to clear those arteries to take the blockage, the clogging away from the arteries.
segments.zh: 如果情况非常严重，有时人们必须做心脏手术，疏通这些动脉，把堵塞物清除掉。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that is to clog something up or something is clogged up.
segments.zh: 所以那就是 to clog something up，或者说某样东西被堵住了。

segments.en: Now moving on, when we were giving suggestions, we said, all right, well, how about pizza or maybe some fried chicken?
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，当我们提出建议时，我们说，好吧，好吧，披萨或一些炸鸡怎么样？

segments.en: Better yet, let's order some hot dogs.
segments.zh: 要不干脆点热狗！

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now this is a great phrase, as you say, Marco, for offering a suggestion.
segments.zh: 现在，正如您所说，这是一个很好的短语，用于提供建议。

segments.en: You could say, I think we should eat hamburgers.
segments.zh: 你可以说，我想我们应该吃汉堡包。

segments.en: Better yet.
segments.zh: 更好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what does this mean?
segments.zh: 那么，这是什么意思？

segments.en: This means I actually had a better idea while I was telling you my other idea.
segments.zh: 这意味着当我告诉你我的其他想法时，我实际上有一个更好的主意。

segments.en: So it can be used in the middle of a sentence like here, right?
segments.zh: 所以它可以像这里一样在句子中间使用，对吧？

segments.en: It's kind of like an interjection.
segments.zh: 这有点像感叹词。

segments.en: Better yet, you know what?
segments.zh: 更好的是，你知道吗？

segments.en: Let's get some pizza.
segments.zh: 让我们来点披萨吧。

segments.en: So it's better than the idea you just had.
segments.zh: 所以它比你刚才的想法要好。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So let's go swimming.
segments.zh: 所以我们去游泳吧。

segments.en: Better yet, let's go play basketball.
segments.zh: 更好的是，我们去打篮球。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So towards the end, our friend said, you know what?
segments.zh: 所以到最后，我们的朋友说，你知道吗？

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: What does that mean?
segments.zh: 那是什么意思？

segments.en: What does this phrase mean?
segments.zh: 这句话是什么意思？

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: It's an interesting phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个有趣的短语。

segments.en: This is basically a way of saying I can do nothing to change you.
segments.zh: 这基本上是一种说我无法改变你的方式。

segments.en: You have a bad habit or you have this bad quality and anything I do, it's not going to help.
segments.zh: 你有个坏习惯，或者有这种坏毛病，不管我做什么都没用。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So something that is a lost cause, it means it's hopeless, helpless.
segments.zh: 所以某件事是 a lost cause，意思就是没救了、无可挽回了。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: I cannot do anything to change it.
segments.zh: 我不能做任何事情来改变它。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A lot of great vocab here.
segments.zh: 这里有很多很棒的词汇。

segments.zh: 我们最后再听一遍对话。

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I was thinking of getting a hamburger, fries and a chocolate sundae.
segments.zh: 我倒想点汉堡、薯条和巧克力圣代。

segments.zh: 你垃圾食品吃得太多了。

segments.zh: 这些东西容易堵塞动脉，胆固醇含量也很高。

segments.zh: 反正我好像怎么吃都不胖，无所谓。

segments.zh: 这不仅仅是关于发胖与否。

segments.zh: 要不干脆点热狗！

segments.en: You're a lost cause.
segments.zh: 你真是无可救药。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So talking about junk food, we took a look at cholesterol.
segments.zh: 所以说到垃圾食品，我们看看胆固醇。

segments.en: Now apparently not all cholesterol is bad.
segments.zh: 现在显然不是所有的胆固醇都是坏的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: There are two kinds of cholesterol, HDLs and LDLs.
segments.zh: 胆固醇有两种，高密度脂蛋白和低密度脂蛋白。

segments.en: One kind is good for you and the other kind is bad for you.
segments.zh: 一种对你有好处，另一种对你有害。

segments.en: So it's important when you talk to your doctor, you ask your doctor if the bad cholesterol is high for you.
segments.zh: 因此，你去看医生的时候，要问一下医生你的坏胆固醇是不是偏高，这一点很重要。

segments.en: Because if it's the good cholesterol that's high, you're probably not going to experience health problems.
segments.zh: 因为如果是好胆固醇很高，你可能不会遇到健康问题。

segments.en: But if you have really high bad cholesterol, then that's something that you should think about when you eat and when you choose the kinds of foods that you eat.
segments.zh: 但如果你的坏胆固醇真的很高，那么你在吃饭和选择你吃的食物种类时应该考虑这一点。

segments.en: So usually, my doctor always used to tell me to not eat so many eggs because eggs are high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 所以通常，我的医生总是告诉我不要吃那么多鸡蛋，因为鸡蛋的胆固醇含量很高。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Red meat and eggs and salty foods I think.
segments.zh: 我认为红肉和鸡蛋和咸食。

segments.en: But generally speaking, I think it's good just to eat a lot of vegetables and to balance out your diet.
segments.zh: 但总的来说，我认为多吃蔬菜并平衡饮食是件好事。

segments.en: So vegetables don't really even have cholesterol.
segments.zh: 所以蔬菜甚至没有胆固醇。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: They have high cholesterol and I think they also have a lot of vitamins and minerals that your body needs.
segments.zh: 它们有高胆固醇，我觉得它们也有很多你身体需要的维生素和矿物质。

segments.en: It's very, very interesting because actually all food that is usually very, very delicious is high in cholesterol or high in calories.
segments.zh: 这非常非常有趣，因为实际上所有非常非常美味的食物都含有高胆固醇或高热量。

segments.en: It's bad for you.
segments.zh: 这对你不好。

segments.en: It's basically junk food.
segments.zh: 基本上是垃圾食品。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So potato chips, hot dogs, pizza, fried chicken, all of these delicious foods, they're all considered junk food and they're all really bad for you.
segments.zh: 所以薯片、热狗、比萨饼、炸鸡，所有这些美味的食物，它们都被认为是垃圾食品，它们都对你很不利。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's a very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Now there are certain local types of junk food that people consider to be junk food.
segments.zh: 现在有一些当地的垃圾食品，人们认为是垃圾食品。

segments.en: Like for example, if you go maybe to the Middle East, you'll have the wraps, right?
segments.zh: 比如，如果你去中东，你就能吃到卷饼，对吧？

segments.en: That could be considered a type of junk food.
segments.zh: 这可以被认为是一种垃圾食品。

segments.en: I guess.
segments.zh: 我想是吧。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Because it's fast, it's greasy.
segments.zh: 因为速度快，油腻。

segments.en: It is pretty greasy.
segments.zh: 它很油腻。

segments.en: All this delicious, like a shawarma wrap.
segments.zh: 这些都很美味，比如沙瓦玛卷饼。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So maybe you can let us know what local type of junk food you have.
segments.zh: 所以也许你可以让我们知道你有什么当地的垃圾食品。

segments.en: This is mostly American, burgers, fries, hot dogs.
segments.zh: 这主要是美国的，汉堡，薯条，热狗。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。
